title: t1: count of tokens in the same class as the last token (mlp0 -> head 1.1 -> mlp1)
label: verified (local-full, full precision)
behavior: Input BOS + 6 tokens from {do, lo, po, to, vo}; the model outputs one digit at the last position.
summary: The model splits the five symbols into two classes, A = {lo, vo} and B = {do, po, to}, and outputs how many of the 6 input tokens (the last one included) belong to the same class as the last token. The circuit is mlp0 (per-position work at each token position), head 1.1 (from the last position attends equally to BOS and to every same-class token, so the BOS weight is 1/(1+count)), and mlp1 (at the last position turns that into the digit). Heads 0.0, 0.1 and 1.0 play no part. All numbers are from local-full at full precision.
pseudocode:
A = {lo, vo}; B = {do, po, to}
class(t) = A if t in A else B          # mlp0, at every token position
count = #{ i in 1..6 : class(x_i) == class(x_6) }   # head 1.1 from the last position: equal attention on BOS and same-class tokens -> BOS weight 1/(1+count)
output digit = count                   # mlp1 at the last position

claims.text: The model does the behaviour deterministically (clean accuracy 1.0 on 128 inputs).
The function is: number of input tokens in the same class as the last token, with classes {lo, vo} and {do, po, to}. The Python version agrees with the model on 200/200 held-out inputs.
Head 1.1 is necessary: resample-ablating it leaves 0.0 of the clean metric; the other three heads each leave 1.0.
mlp0 and mlp1 are both necessary: resample-ablating either leaves 0.0 of the clean metric.
Heads 0.0, 0.1 and 1.0 play no part: jointly mean-ablating all three leaves 1.0 of the clean metric; with everything outside {mlp0, 1.1, mlp1} ablated the model keeps accuracy 1.0.

Head 1.1 at the last position attends only to BOS and same-class tokens with equal weight: when the last token is the only member of its class, 0.5 goes to BOS, 0.5 to itself and 0 to the five other-class tokens.
mlp1 does its work only at the last position (patching it there alone restores 1.0); mlp0 works at each of the six token positions (0.29-0.36 each) and not at BOS (0.0).
After layer 0 the answer is not yet at the last position (patching resid_post.0 at pos 6 alone restores 0.36); after layer 1 it is (1.0). So the count is moved to the last position in layer 1.
Ablating the circuit {mlp0, 1.1, mlp1} drops the metric to 0.0015 of clean (accuracy 0.25); all three checks beat their null distributions.

nodes.label: head 1.1: last pos attends to BOS + same-class tokens; BOS weight = 1/(1+count)

edges.label: class at each position (query and key)

limitations: What mlp0 writes was not read out directly. That it is a class mark is inferred from the attention rule of 1.1 (E0009) plus mlp0 being needed at every token position (E0012, E0013). Path patching from mlp0 into 1.1's query/key was attempted and the primitive errored for an MLP sender, so the mlp0 -> 1.1 edge is not separately measured.
The split of mlp1's role (decode 1/(1+count) to a digit) is inferred from the attention weights and position patching; the numeric encoding in 1.1's output was not measured.

E0009 used inputs where the last token is alone in its class; the general 1/(1+count) weighting is consistent with the exploratory mean pattern in E0005 but only the count = 1 case was pre-registered.
V0001's three random same-size ablation sets all returned 1.0; with only 6 components the random control is coarse.
open_questions: Do heads 0.0, 0.1 and 1.0 compute anything coherent, or are they pure distractors?
Which side(s) of head 1.1 (query, key, value) read mlp0's output?
